use: Happy anticipation of something coming up.

example.romaji: Ashita no ryokou, wakuwaku suru ne!
example.ja: 明日の旅行、ワクワクするね！
example.english: So excited for tomorrow's trip!

examplePolite.romaji: Ashita no ryokou, wakuwaku shimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 明日の旅行、ワクワクしますね。
examplePolite.english: I'm really looking forward to tomorrow's trip.

notes: Wakuwaku shite nemurenai = too excited to sleep.

use: Ongoing irritation or impatience from people, waiting or stress.

example.ja: 電車が来なくてイライラする。
example.english: The train isn't coming and it's driving me nuts.

examplePolite.ja: 電車が来なくてイライラします。
examplePolite.english: The train isn't coming, and it's frustrating.

notes: Iraira shinaide = don't get so worked up.

use: When something falls short of what you hoped.

example.romaji: Ame de shiai ga chuushi ni natte, gakkari shita.
example.ja: 雨で試合が中止になって、がっかりした。
example.english: The game got rained off. What a letdown.

examplePolite.romaji: Ame de shiai ga chuushi ni natte, gakkari shimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 雨で試合が中止になって、がっかりしました。
examplePolite.english: I was disappointed the game was cancelled for rain.

notes: Said to someone's face (anata ni gakkari shita) it's a harsh rebuke.

use: The relief when a worry ends, or the calm of feeling at home.

example.ja: 無事でほっとしたよ。
example.english: I'm so relieved you're okay.

examplePolite.ja: 無事でほっとしました。
examplePolite.english: I was relieved you were safe.

notes: Hotto suru basho = a place where you can relax.

english: a bit early; earlier than usual
use: Mostly hayame ni: doing something ahead of time to be safe.

example.ja: 混むから、早めに出よう。
example.english: It'll be crowded, so let's leave a bit early.

examplePolite.ja: 混みますから、早めに出ましょう。
examplePolite.english: It gets crowded, so let's leave a little early.

notes: The opposite is osome (a bit late). -me after an adjective means 'on the X side': ookime (biggish).

english: just barely; at the last minute; cutting it close
use: Right at the limit of time, space or money: girigiri ma ni atta (just made it).

example.ja: 終電、ギリギリ間に合った！
example.english: I just barely made the last train!

examplePolite.romaji: Shuuden ni girigiri ma ni aimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 終電にギリギリ間に合いました。
examplePolite.english: I just made the last train.

notes: Girigiri made = until the last possible moment: girigiri made neru (sleep till the last minute).

use: A common excuse for being out of touch: batabata shiteta (things have been crazy).

example.ja: 今週はバタバタしてた。
example.english: This week's been crazy.

examplePolite.ja: 今週はバタバタしていました。
examplePolite.english: This week has been hectic.

notes: Also the sound of flapping, or of feet running around.

english: take it easy; relax; be laid-back
use: Relaxing with no rush; also describes an easygoing person or place.

example.romaji: Shuumatsu wa ie de nonbiri shitai.
example.ja: 週末は家でのんびりしたい。
example.english: I want to take it easy at home this weekend.

examplePolite.romaji: Shuumatsu wa ie de nonbiri shitai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 週末は家でのんびりしたいです。
examplePolite.english: I'd like to relax at home this weekend.

notes: Nonbiri shita hito = an easygoing (or slow-moving) person.

use: Stresses how small a number or amount is, often with dake.

example.ja: たった五分で終わったよ。
example.english: It only took five minutes.

examplePolite.ja: たった五分で終わりましたよ。
examplePolite.english: It took just five minutes.

notes: Goes right before the number, while dake follows it: tatta sen'en dake (just 1,000 yen).

english: just a; a mere; only a little
use: Comes before a noun to make it small: hon no sukoshi (just a tiny bit).

example.ja: ほんの少しだけちょうだい。
example.english: Just give me a tiny bit.

examplePolite.ja: ほんの少しだけください。
examplePolite.english: Just a little, please.

notes: Hon no kimochi desu = it's just a small token (said when giving a gift).

use: Before a noun: a small, casual thing, like chotto shita omiyage (a little gift).

example.romaji: Chotto shita mondai ga atte, okureta.
example.ja: ちょっとした問題があって、遅れた。
example.english: There was a small problem, so I was late.

examplePolite.romaji: Chotto shita mondai ga atte, okuremashita.
examplePolite.ja: ちょっとした問題があって、遅れました。
examplePolite.english: There was a minor problem, so I was late.

notes: Can flip to 'quite a': chotto shita yuumeijin (quite a celebrity).

english: a little; somewhat; more or less
use: Often in 'even if a bit...' and in hedges: tashou no okure (some delay).

example.romaji: Tashou takakute mo, kore ga ii.
example.ja: 多少高くても、これがいい。
example.english: Even if it's a bit pricey, I want this one.

examplePolite.romaji: Tashou takakute mo, kore ga ii desu.
examplePolite.ja: 多少高くても、これがいいです。
examplePolite.english: Even if it costs a little more, I'd like this one.

notes: Sounds a bit more formal than sukoshi or chotto.

english: more and more; quickly; one after another
use: Fast, steady progress or increase; dondon tabete urges someone to dig in.

example.romaji: Nihongo, dondon jouzu ni natteru ne.
example.ja: 日本語、どんどん上手になってるね。
example.english: Your Japanese is getting better and better.

examplePolite.romaji: Nihongo ga dondon jouzu ni natte imasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 日本語がどんどん上手になっていますね。
examplePolite.english: Your Japanese is improving quickly.

notes: Also a banging or drumming sound.

english: little by little; a bit at a time
use: Gradual progress, or doing something in small portions.

example.ja: 少しずつ慣れてきたよ。
example.english: I'm getting used to it little by little.

examplePolite.ja: 少しずつ慣れてきました。
examplePolite.english: I'm gradually getting used to it.

notes: -zutsu means 'each' or 'at a time': hitotsu zutsu (one each).

use: Something already true keeps growing: masumasu samuku naru.

example.ja: 説明聞いたら、ますますわからなくなった。
example.english: After the explanation I was even more confused.

examplePolite.romaji: Setsumei o kiitara, masumasu wakaranaku narimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 説明を聞いたら、ますますわからなくなりました。
examplePolite.english: The explanation left me even more confused.

notes: Dondon stresses speed; masumasu stresses growing degree.

english: even more; further; on top of that
use: Raises the degree of something already said; a bit more formal than motto.

example.romaji: Ame ga sara ni tsuyoku natta.
example.ja: 雨がさらに強くなった。
example.english: The rain got even heavier.

examplePolite.romaji: Ame ga sara ni tsuyoku narimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 雨がさらに強くなりました。
examplePolite.english: The rain has become even heavier.

notes: At the start of a sentence it means 'moreover', common in news and ads.

use: Mou juubun politely turns down more food or help.

example.ja: もう十分だよ、ありがとう。
example.english: That's plenty, thanks.

examplePolite.ja: もう十分です、ありがとうございます。
examplePolite.english: I've had plenty, thank you.

notes: The same kanji read juppun means ten minutes.

use: Very nearly all or complete: hobo owatta, hobo mainichi.

example.ja: 宿題、ほぼ終わった。
example.english: My homework's almost done.

examplePolite.ja: 宿題はほぼ終わりました。
examplePolite.english: I've nearly finished my homework.

notes: Close to hotondo (almost all); hobo mainichi = nearly every day.

use: Mostly kanzen ni before a verb or adjective: totally, 100%.

example.ja: 完全に道に迷った。
example.english: We're completely lost.

examplePolite.ja: 完全に道に迷いました。
examplePolite.english: I've got completely lost.

notes: Sukkari is softer and about change; kanzen ni is blunt and absolute.

use: A generous, full amount, often of food, time or sleep.

example.ja: 昨日はたっぷり寝た。
example.english: I got plenty of sleep last night.

examplePolite.ja: 昨日はたっぷり寝ました。
examplePolite.english: I slept plenty last night.

notes: Jikan wa tappuri aru = there's plenty of time.
